Container.Name: Unraid-Home
Container.Overview:
Self-populating homepage for your Unraid server. Scans Docker for containers and shows each one as a tile with its WebUI link, icon and status. Edit mode (from your home network) lets you rename, regroup, pin and hide tiles, add links and pages, and pick themes. Optional: login with authenticator sign-in, alerts (ntfy, Gotify, Discord, webhook, email), uptime and update badges, server stats, and automation for Nginx Proxy Manager and Cloudflare Tunnel so your apps get internet addresses automatically. All settings are optional.
Almost everything is set on the homepage itself: click Settings (home network only). What you set there is saved in /config/options.json. Only the few values on this template page that the container needs before it can start (the Docker address, proxy trust, the password and the mapped folders) stay here.
Email alerts with Gmail need an app password (https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords), not your normal Google password.
Built entirely by AI (Claude, by Anthropic). Features are tested, but not every situation has been, so do your own due diligence before exposing it to the internet: keep the login on, use a strong password and 2FA, and review your Cloudflare, proxy and firewall settings. Use at your own risk.
Container.Changes:
### 2026-11-27 — 1.16.0 - Bookmarks (the file and the extension) now start with a bookmark to the homepage itself. - The homepage's own proxy host is recognised on the Proxies page, whatever it's called, and Add all / Remove all leave it alone.
### 2026-11-26 — 1.15.2 (1.12.0 to 1.15.2) - A browser extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox keeps a bookmarks folder of your apps up to date by itself while you're on your home network; download it from the bottom of the page or the Bookmarks window. - A Security overview on the Visitors page: a checklist of how the page is protected, current lockouts with Unlock, attackers and sign-ins from the internet. - The activity list shows allowed access as well as blocked, with Load more; click any address to see who it belongs to and what it did. - The version number at the bottom of the page. - Clearer about which settings you need when your Cloudflare tunnel already works: just the main domain (and Nginx Proxy Manager's login for the Proxies page).
### 2026-11-14 — 1.11.0 - Rename an app's internet address on the Proxies page (npm.example.com instead of nginxproxymanager.example.com), with its Nginx Proxy Manager host renamed to match.
### 2026-10-22 — 1.10.2 (1.10.0 to 1.10.2) - Download every app as a browser bookmarks file, in one "Server" folder, from a Bookmarks link beside the clock. - Proxy hosts that forward to the container name count as working, so their internet addresses appear in the bookmarks file and the internet view.
### 2026-10-20 — 1.9.2 (1.6.2 to 1.9.2) - Full control of Nginx Proxy Manager from a Proxies page: create, remove, Add all missing, Remove all, "no proxy" and a per-app Auto-create choice, with filters and automatic-creation controls. - The internet view only shows apps that really have a proxy host, and when signed in can switch to your home-network links; its tiles show the address they open. - Typing on the Settings page no longer loses focus; the icon loads from the main branch of Unraid-CA-Apps.
### 2026-10-19 — 1.6.1 (1.1.0 to 1.6.1) - Settings now live on a Settings page on the homepage, grouped and explained (saved in /config/options.json). The template keeps only what the container needs to start (Docker address, proxy trust, password, mapped folders); anything you already set is still used. - Your home network no longer needs a login by default (REQUIRE_LOGIN_LAN=true restores it); separate sign-in timeouts for home and internet. - Visitor history and a Visitors page (page loads, sign-ins, blocked requests, scans, apps opened, per-app availability) kept as plain files in /config/analytics; connection status for Nginx Proxy Manager and Cloudflare. - A clock beside the page title: digital, analog or both.
### 2026-10-18 — 1.0.1 (1.0.0 and 1.0.1) - First stable release, followed by security review fixes (proxy-header handling, lockout limits) and socket-proxy setup docs.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the homepage is served on

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Used to discover containers (and, only if you turn on Container controls, to start/stop/restart them). Note: the read-only flag does not limit what the Docker API allows.

Config.Name: Unraid templates
Config.Description: Optional. Lets the hover summaries use each app's Overview text from its Unraid template. Read-only; only the name, repository, overview and category are read.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Stores your settings, tile overrides, custom links and visitor history

Config.Name: Update status file
Config.Description: Optional. Lets tiles show an Update badge for containers Unraid says are out of date. Read-only.

Config.Name: Disk stats: array
Config.Description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show array usage.

Config.Name: Disk stats: cache
Config.Description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show cache usage.

Config.Name: Password
Config.Description: Login password (12+ characters). Leave blank to have one generated on first start; it is printed once in this container's log and stored only as a salted hash. This is the one setting the Settings page cannot change; use Change password there instead once the container is running.

Config.Name: Docker address
Config.Description: Where to ask about containers. Leave as-is when the Docker socket above is mapped in. Use tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375 if you run a socket proxy instead (recommended when this page is reachable from the internet). Settings page shows this one read-only.

Config.Name: Trust proxy headers
Config.Description: On (default) believes the address headers from a reverse proxy or Cloudflare tunnel on your network, so the real visitor address and country are recorded. Turn off only if nothing in front of this page adds those headers. Settings page shows this one read-only.
